entries.name: Khmer Empire (Angkor)
entries.region: Mainland Southeast Asia (Cambodia, plus Laos, Thailand, southern Vietnam)
entries.settlement: sprawling low-density temple-cities around baray reservoirs; Angkor was a 1,000-sq-km urban zone
trade: rice and fish to China
Chinese ceramics and silk in
elephants, resin, lacquer and gold out
entries.beliefs: devaraja (god-king) cult, Shaivite then Mahayana Buddhist under Jayavarman VII; ancestors and neak ta spirits
entries.fell_by: Ayutthaya sacked Angkor 1431; court relocated to Longvek then Phnom Penh
entries.notes: One part city, one part water machine - the baray reservoirs fed thousands of hectares of rice. Angkor Wat remains the largest religious building on Earth.

entries.name: Đại Việt (Lý-Trần-Lê)
entries.settlement: walled towns and dense river-delta villages; Thang Long (Hanoi) capital from 1010
trade: rice and silk out
Chinese ceramics and copper in
tribute trade with Song, Yuan and Ming
entries.beliefs: Mahayana Buddhism + Confucian statecraft + ancestor worship; village đình spirits
entries.fell_by: not fallen as a people; Nguyen-hue monarchy ended 1945, state continues as Vietnam
entries.notes: Beat three Mongol invasions (1258, 1285, 1288) with river navies - Trần Hưng Đạo at Bạch Đằng is the national epic.

entries.name: Pagan Kingdom (Bagan)
entries.settlement: walled capital at Bagan on the Irrawaddy; plain of merit-making stupas
trade: rice, elephants and teak out
Chinese porcelain in
overland Yunnan route plus coastal trade
entries.beliefs: Theravada Buddhism (Anawrahta's conversion c. 1057); nat spirits folded into the Buddhist pantheon
entries.fell_by: Mongol/Yuan invasions; Bagan sacked 1287
entries.notes: The Bagan plain holds 2,000+ surviving stupas - the densest Buddhist archaeological landscape on Earth. Ananda and Shwezigon anchor it.

entries.name: Ayutthaya Kingdom
entries.settlement: island capital ringed by three rivers; cosmopolitan port with Portuguese, Japanese and Persian quarters
trade: rice, tin, elephants and teak out
European firearms and textiles in
Persian, Chinese and Portuguese merchants
entries.beliefs: Theravada Buddhism + Hindu court ritual; kingship descended from devaraja tradition
entries.fell_by: Burmese sack of Ayutthaya 1767; capital moved to Thonburi then Bangkok
entries.notes: A port city that spoke every language; its 1767 destruction made salvaged Buddha heads the national wound Bangkok still carries.

entries.name: Srivijaya Empire
entries.settlement: riverine entrepots at the Musi mouth (Palembang); Muaro Jambi temple zone upstream
trade: taxed the Strait of Malacca choke point
spices, aromatics and forest products out
Indian and Chinese porcelain in
entries.beliefs: Mahayana/Vajrayana Buddhism - patron of Buddhist learning; Chinese pilgrim Yijing studied here 671-695
entries.fell_by: Chola raid 1025; faded as Melayu and Jambi rose; absorbed by Majapahit by 14th century
entries.notes: A choke-point empire: whoever held the Musi mouth taxed every ship between India and China.

entries.name: Majapahit Empire
entries.region: Java plus eastern Indonesia and the Malay archipelago
entries.settlement: capital at Trowulan - red-brick palaces, canals and bathing tanks (Candi Tikus)
trade: archipelago cloves and nutmeg to China
Gajah Mada's Palapa oath 1336 claimed 'Nusantara' (all archipelago)
entries.beliefs: Hindu-Buddhist Siwa-Buddha syncretism; tantric royal courts; Nagarakretagama (1365) as imperial litany
entries.fell_by: succession wars; coastal Demak seized Java's ports c. 1478-1527; last Hindu court fled to Bali
entries.notes: Indonesia's motto 'Bhinneka Tunggal Ika' (Unity in Diversity) is quoted straight from a Majapahit poem.

entries.name: Malacca Sultanate
subsistence: entrepot trade at the strait's narrowest point
entries.settlement: fortified port city with syahbandar-run foreign quarters (Gujaratis, Chinese, Tamils, Javanese)
trade: the hinge of the spice trade
tin, elephants and sandalwood out
Indian textiles and Chinese porcelain in
entries.beliefs: Islam (conversion c. 1400-1409); Sunni Shafi'i; cosmopolitan port pluralism under Islamic law
entries.fell_by: Portuguese conquest 1511 (Afonso de Albuquerque)
entries.notes: Whoever holds Malacca holds the strait - the reason it passed Portuguese to Dutch to British hands.

entries.name: Sukhothai Kingdom
entries.settlement: walled capital, open grid, monasteries donated by kings
trade: Sangkhalok ceramics across SE Asia and to China
rice and lacquer out
entries.beliefs: Theravada Buddhism; paternal kingship (dhammaraja) - 'a father to his people'
entries.fell_by: absorbed by Ayutthaya 1438
entries.notes: Ramkhamhaeng is credited with the Thai script (c. 1283); the Sukhothai inscription is the oldest surviving Thai writing.

entries.name: Champa
entries.settlement: chain of coastal principalities (Amaravati, Vijaya, Panduranga) - never one state
trade: pepper, aloe wood and sandalwood out
maritime middlemen between India, Arabia and China
entries.beliefs: devaraja Shiva cult; later syncretic Hinduism and Islam; ancestor and rice-field spirits
entries.fell_by: Vijaya conquered by Le Thanh Tong 1471; Panduranga annexed by Vietnam 1832
entries.notes: 'Champa' is a Chinese label for a string of port-states, not a unified kingdom - each principality was its own world.

entries.name: Lan Xang ('Land of a Million Elephants')
entries.settlement: capitals moved between Luang Prabang and Vientiane; villages vastly outnumber towns
trade: elephants and cardamom out
overland trade with Yunnan and Ayutthaya
entries.beliefs: Theravada Buddhism; naga (Phaya Nak) guardian myth; phi animist spirits
entries.fell_by: split into Luang Prabang, Vientiane and Champasak 1707; vassal of Siam by 1779
entries.notes: Mountain geography means the temple, not the palace, is the permanent architecture - almost every substantial brick structure is religious.

entries.name: Sailendra Dynasty
entries.settlement: central Javanese temple-courts; later Srivijaya (Palembang)
crafts: volcanic andesite masonry (Borobudur: 2M+ fitted blocks, no mortar)
trade: tied Java's rice wealth to Srivijaya shipping
entries.beliefs: Mahayana Buddhism - Borobudur is a walk-through 3D mandala for pilgrimage
entries.fell_by: absorbed by the rival Sanjaya Hindu line; last king Balaputra expelled to Srivijaya c. 850
entries.notes: Built the world's largest Buddhist monument without mortar - and then quietly vanished from the record.

entries.name: Mataram Sultanate (Islamic Java)
entries.settlement: court cities - Kotagede, then Kraton Yogyakarta and Surakarta (both still extant)
monuments: Kraton of Yogyakarta and Surakarta compounds
trade: teak and rice out
forced contracts with the Dutch East India Company (VOC), tightening coercion
entries.beliefs: Islam fused with kejawen Javanese mysticism; Wali Songo legacy; court kawula-gusti (servant-lord) philosophy
entries.fell_by: Treaty of Giyanti 1755 split it into Yogyakarta and Surakarta under Dutch suzerainty
entries.notes: Sultan Agung besieged Batavia twice (1628, 1629) - the largest Javanese campaign ever mounted against the VOC.

entries.name: Aceh Sultanate
entries.settlement: capitals at Banda Aceh; fortified pepper port; the 'Veranda of Mecca'
trade: pepper to Europe and Arabia
dominated strait trade under Iskandar Muda
diplomatic alliance with the Ottomans
entries.beliefs: Islam - Shafi'i with strong Sufi orders (Syattariyah); four consecutive female sultans reigned 1641-1699
entries.fell_by: Dutch Aceh War 1873-1904; last sultan deposed 1903
entries.notes: Held out against the Dutch for 31 years - the costliest colonial war in the Indies, and the source of Acehnese separatism to this day.

entries.name: Brunei Sultanate
entries.settlement: stilt-city Kampong Ayer on the Brunei River - continuously settled for centuries
trade: camphor, pearls, bird's nests and sago out
at its 1500s peak it claimed Borneo, Luzon and the Sulu coast
entries.beliefs: Sunni Islam - Malay-Islam monarchy; adat bersendi syarak (custom rests on Islamic law)
entries.fell_by: not fallen; absolute monarchy continues, now oil-financed
entries.notes: One of the oldest continuously ruling monarchies; at its 16th-century peak Brunei made Manila a tributary.

entries.name: Demak Sultanate
entries.settlement: port city at Demak on the Java Sea; Java's first Islamic political center
trade: entrepot on the spice route after Malacca fell to Portugal 1511
entries.beliefs: Islam - spread by the Wali Songo (nine saints) using wayang, gamelan and syncretic preaching
entries.fell_by: defeated by Pajang c. 1549-1560; remnant moved to Kalinyamat
entries.notes: The Wali Songo converted Java with shadow puppets and kept the gamelan - Islam by art, not by conquest.

entries.name: Sulu Sultanate
entries.region: Sulu Archipelago and north Borneo (Philippines, Malaysia)
entries.settlement: stilt coastal towns (Buansa, Maimbung); fortified kuta; pearl fisheries
trade: pearls and trepang to China
controlled Sulu Sea tolls
major slave-raiding by 18th-19th century
entries.beliefs: Sunni Islam (Shafi'i with Tausug adat); sultans claimed Arab Sharif descent; Paduka Pahala died in China 1417 and is honored at a Dezhou shrine
entries.fell_by: Spain occupied Jolo 1876; Carpenter Agreement 1915 ended the sultan's temporal power under the US
entries.notes: Pearls and gunboats: Sulu's fleets raided from Luzon to Borneo for four hundred years, and the Sabah claim still echoes.

entries.name: Minangkabau
entries.settlement: village (nagari) republics clustered around grand houses; Pagaruyung as royal capital
trade: gold and coffee out (16th-19th century)
rantau merchant networks spread across the entire archipelago
entries.beliefs: Islam - adat basandi syarak, syarak basandi Kitabullah (custom rests on Islamic law); matrilineal clan (suku) ancestor worship
entries.fell_by: not fallen; Pagaruyung's last independence ended in the Padri War 1821-1837
entries.notes: The world's largest matrilineal society - property and clan pass through the mother, while men take public office.

entries.name: Bugis
entries.region: South Sulawesi (plus diaspora across the archipelago)
entries.settlement: seaport courts at Bone, Luwu, Wajo and Soppeng; phinisi schooners; diasporas in Riau, Johor, Selangor
trade: archipelago spice and rice entrepot
Bugis mercenary-trader networks reached northern Australia (trepang fleets)
entries.beliefs: Islam over To Ri olo (the old way); bissu gender-liminal priest-shamans; La Galigo epic cosmology
entries.fell_by: not fallen; Bone's monarchy ended 1960; Bugis culture thrives
entries.notes: The La Galigo is one of the longest epics ever written - several times the length of the Iliad - and still partly recited.

entries.name: Balinese (Gelgel and Klungkung)
entries.settlement: rice villages built around temple networks (banjar); Gelgel then Klungkung as royal capitals
trade: rice, cotton cloth and slaves to Java and Lombok
Dutch pressure from the 1840s
entries.beliefs: Hindu Dharma (Agama Hindu Bali) - ancestor worship, tri hita karana (god-human-nature harmony); four-fold caste (wangsa)
entries.fell_by: Dutch puputan (ritual mass suicide) of Denpasar 1906 and Klungkung 1908
entries.notes: When Majapahit fell, Java's Hindu court decamped wholesale to Bali - the island preserved Javanese-Hindu civilization intact.

entries.name: Toraja
entries.settlement: hill villages of tongkonan longhouses; no state, organized by aristocratic clan alliances (puang)
trade: ritual buffalo market (a sacred economy)
highland isolation preserved custom; coffee now exports
entries.beliefs: Aluk To Dolo ('the way of the ancestors') - Rambu Solo' funerals with buffalo sacrifice; soul journeys; Rambu Tuka' life ceremonies
entries.fell_by: not fallen; formally under Dutch rule from 1906; culture thrives on tourism and remittances
entries.notes: Funerals are the economy - elite families sacrifice dozens of water buffalo, and status is measured in buffalo, literally.

entries.name: Batak Peoples (Toba, Karo, Mandailing)
entries.settlement: clan villages (huta) around Lake Toba; exogamous patrilineal clans (marga)
trade: coffee and resin via the Barus port
interior raiding and trade tied to coastal Malay states (historic)
entries.beliefs: pre-Christian Batak religion - Debata (supreme), tondi (soul), marga ancestors; now mostly Christian (post-1860s missions), partly Muslim (Mandailing)
entries.fell_by: Dutch conquest of Toba 1907; Sisingamangaraja XII killed at Laguboti
entries.notes: Ulos cloth changes hands at every Batak rite - birth, wedding, death. Batak genealogies are sung, not written.

entries.name: Dayak Peoples (Ngaju, Iban, Kenyah)
entries.settlement: river longhouses (rumah betang) 50-300 m; Iban 'sea Dayak' raided coasts; Ngaju upriver courts
trade: birds' nests, eaglewood (gaharu) and camphor out via Banjarmasin and Pontianak
entries.beliefs: Kaharingan (Ngaju) animism - Mahatara creator; ngayau headhunting captured life-force for rice fertility; balian shaman mediumship
entries.fell_by: not fallen; Dutch and British protectorates from the 19th century; autonomy within Indonesia and Malaysia
entries.notes: Ngayau was cosmological, not cruelty - heads farmed the fields with borrowed life-force. Now UNESCO recognizes Dayak weaving and chant.

entries.name: Ifugao
entries.settlement: mountain villages along 2,000-year-old hand-built rice terraces; no central state; kadangyan elite vs tagu commoners
trade: rice to the lowlands; salt in; never conquered by Spain, the US or Japan
entries.beliefs: anito ancestor worship; mumbaki priests; bulul rice-granary guardians; head-taking (historic)
entries.fell_by: not fallen; Spanish failure, US peace pacts, then highland autonomy within the Philippines
entries.notes: 10,000+ hectares of mountain slopes, terraced by hand and still irrigated by ancient channels - a UNESCO World Heritage engineering marvel.

entries.name: Tagalog Barangays
entries.region: Luzon (Manila Bay, Laguna de Bay), Philippines
entries.settlement: barangay boat-polities (30-100 households) led by a datu; rajanates at Maynila and Tondo behind river-mouth kuta forts
monuments: Maynila and Tondo kuta forts (pre-Spanish, long vanished)
trade: gold, beeswax and textiles with Brunei, China, Siam and Borneo
Maynila was a Brunei-backed Muslim port by 1570
entries.beliefs: Bathala (creator) + anito spirits; babaylan shamans; Islam arriving in Maynila and Tondo c. 1500
entries.fell_by: Spanish conquest 1570-1571 (Goiti, de Salcedo); Legazpi founded Manila 1571
entries.notes: The Laguna Copperplate Inscription (900 CE) proves early Philippine literacy - written in Old Javanese with Kawi script.

entries.name: Butuan Rajanate
entries.settlement: river-mouth rajanate; balangay boat yards; no walled capital known - power lived on the water
crafts: Butuan goldwork (10th-century funerary masks and betel sets)
trade: gold and forest products to Song China (tributary missions 11th century)
porcelain and bronze in
entries.beliefs: Indianized - Hindu-Buddhist court cults; an ivory seal with a Kawi inscription depicting a goddess was found here
entries.fell_by: absorbed into Sulu and Mindanao sultanates by the 1500s; Magellan met Rajah Siagu 1521
entries.notes: The balangay - plank-built edge-pegged boats carbon-dated to 320 CE - makes Butuan one of Asia's oldest seafaring cultures.

entries.name: Maranao
entries.settlement: lakeside torogan royal houses; never conquered by Spain; a self-governing darul Islam
trade: rice and lake fish to Sulu and Borneo
direct ties to Brunei and Sulu markets
entries.beliefs: Sunni Islam - Maranao adat; Darangen epic cosmology; rido (blood-feud) ethic historically governed justice
entries.fell_by: not fallen to Spain (Spain never held Lanao); US conquest 1899-1903; Marawi 2017 siege tested resilience
entries.notes: The Darangen is one of the longest surviving oral epics - sung at feasts, it encodes Maranao law, genealogy and cosmology.

entries.name: Sundanese (Pajajaran)
entries.settlement: court at Pakuan (Bogor) - walled kraton ringed by sacred forest and ladang fields
dwellings: imah stilt houses with badak heuay saddle roofs
trade: pepper and forest products via the port of Sunda Kalapa
entries.beliefs: Hindu-Buddhist Sunda, then Islam after Pajajaran's fall; Sunda Wiwitan folk strain survives among the Baduy inland
entries.fell_by: Pakuan sacked by Banten sultanate 1579; Sunda absorbed
entries.notes: The inland Kanekes (Baduy) of Banten still live almost entirely outside the modern economy - a living window on this world.

entries.name: Shan States
entries.settlement: fortified saopha towns (Hsipaw, Kengtung, Mong Nai); hereditary lords owing nominal fealty to Burma
trade: tea and ponies along the Burma-Yunnan road
opium historically
silk north to China
entries.beliefs: Theravada Buddhism underpinned by wan (village guardian) spirit cults
entries.fell_by: sawbwa powers abolished 1959 as independent Burma consolidated; states became Myanmar divisions
entries.notes: 'Saopha' means lord of the sky; Shan opium money bankrolled half of Burma's 20th-century politics.

entries.name: Mon (Hanthawaddy/Pegu)
entries.settlement: port cities - Pegu, Martaban, Thaton; river-mouth Mon power
trade: alum, tin and ivory out
Arab, Indian and Chinese merchants at Thaton and Pegu
entries.beliefs: Theravada Buddhism - Mon monks carried the Dhamma north to Pagan; spirit cults
entries.fell_by: Alaungpaya's sack of Pegu 1757
entries.notes: The Mon taught the Burmese Buddhism - their final defeat ended a thousand years of Mon statehood.

entries.name: Pyu City-States
entries.settlement: circular walled city-states - Beikthano, Sri Ksetra, Halin
monuments: Sri Ksetra city walls and stupas
trade: Pyu missions reached Tang China (802, 832) - dancers and musicians presented at court
entries.beliefs: early Theravada Buddhism over solar and animist cults
entries.fell_by: Nanzhao raid sacked Sri Ksetra 832; absorbed into emerging Pagan
entries.notes: The Pyu script, undeciphered for a century, has been read from stone and gold fragments - an entire lost literature.

entries.name: Funan
entries.settlement: delta trading state; canal port Oc Eo linked to the capital
trade: transit hub of India-China trade; Roman and Han coins found at Oc Eo
entries.beliefs: Indianized - Vishnu and Shiva adopted into a royal court religion; Kaundinya-Soma origin myth
entries.fell_by: absorbed by Chenla c. 550
entries.notes: The first Indianized state in Southeast Asia - the template every god-king kingdom after it copied.

entries.name: Hmong (Miao)
entries.settlement: ridge villages; patrilineal clan (xeem) system; migrated from Guizhou and Sichuan over 200+ years
dwellings: buffalo-horn-gabled houses (roof beams curve upward like horns)
trade: opium historically; today rice, vegetables and story-cloths for markets; large diaspora in the US and France
entries.beliefs: animism and shamanism - txiv neeb shamans journey to recover lost souls; ancestor re-burial rituals; Shong Lue Yang's 'Mother of Writing' movement 1959-1970
entries.fell_by: not fallen; diaspora after 1975; Shong Lue Yang's Hmong kingdom collapsed 1970
entries.notes: Paj ntaub story-cloths record history pictorially - one of the few textile traditions that narrates like a written chronicle.

entries.name: Karen (Sgaw and Pwo)
entries.settlement: upland stilt villages along ridgelines; no historical state; tributary to Pagan and Ayutthaya; Kayin State since 1952
trade: forest products; teak logging with elephants
entries.beliefs: Y'wa (supreme being) animism under syncretic Buddhism and Christianity (missions from the 1800s)
entries.fell_by: not fallen; armed autonomy struggle inside Myanmar since 1949 (Karen National Union)
entries.notes: Saw/Naw are male/female name prefixes; Karen are famed as the elephant mahouts of the teak forests.

entries.name: Degar (Montagnards: Rhade, Jarai, Bahnar)
entries.settlement: longhouse villages around rong communal houses; no states; the French called them Montagnards
trade: forest products; coffee (20th century); historically isolated between Cham and Vietnamese courts
entries.beliefs: animism - creator Y ang plus village and clan yang spirits; buffalo sacrifices at rong ceremonies
entries.fell_by: not fallen; FULRO autonomy movement 1964-92; displacement continued
entries.notes: UNESCO recognizes the gong culture of the Vietnamese Central Highlands as intangible heritage (2005).

entries.name: Orang Asli (Semang, Senoi, Proto-Malay)
entries.settlement: dispersed jungle hamlets; communal longhouses among some Senoi groups
trade: eaglewood (gaharu), rattan and dammar gum to Malay ports
entries.beliefs: animism - hala' shamans mediate with forest spirits (ruwai)
entries.fell_by: not fallen; enslaved and displaced under Malay sultanates and British rule; now ~150,000 people, Malaysia's poorest group
entries.notes: The Peninsula's original population - three distinct groups speaking some 18 languages.

entries.name: Sama-Bajau (Sea Nomads)
entries.settlement: stilt villages over reefs; lepa houseboats - some families still live aboard; no state, dispersed kinship clusters
trade: sea cucumbers (trepang) to China
pearls to Sulu ports
fish to coastal markets
entries.beliefs: Islam plus sea-spirit appeasement; dukun sea trances; respect for the sacred sea serpent
entries.fell_by: not fallen; progressively settled from the 20th century; rights struggles in Sabah and Sulu
entries.notes: Freedive to 20+ m on one breath; lifelong diving enlarges the spleen - a real, measured genetic adaptation (Science, 2018).
